summary.text: Beacon Tower is Tie clan's Immortal Gu House formed from Beacon Towers scattered across Southern Border. The network lets Southern Border's righteous path move Gu Immortals between towers and close a pursuit net.

claims.text: During the hunt for Shadow Sect remnants, Wu Yong reaches a waiting position with Tie clan’s Immortal Gu House Beacon Tower rather than relying only on Clear Jade Dripping Wind Tiny Bamboo Building’s speed.

Tie clan’s first supreme elder later pitches Beacon Tower together with Chi clan formations against Fang Yuan: the formations buy time, then Beacon Tower teleportation brings killers in. Beacon Tower’s greatest use is similar to Western Desert Xiao clan’s Ten Thousand Li Silk Corridor. The house is made of multiple Beacon Towers that can transport Gu Immortals to each other, and if many towers are linked they can even transport rank eight Gu Immortals. Tie clan had already been trying to plant more towers across Southern Border, but other super forces treated that net as a threat and blocked expansion; when Tie clan promotes the plan again under the Fang Yuan crisis, the other leaders keep silent rather than agree.
Deviation (recorded): this page is filed under gu-houses because Beacon Tower is a named Immortal Gu House. The standing pieces are a transport network across Southern Border, not one fixed map seat.

A Tie clan Gu Immortal again names Immortal Gu House Beacon Tower as a way to ease the Fang Yuan problem, and Wu Yong supports Tie clan building Beacon Towers. Ba clan, Chi Qu You, Luo clan, Hou clan, Chai clan, and others join that support as Southern Border righteous path forces move into true close cooperation.

After that agreement, small groups rush Southern Border to build Beacon Towers. One finished tower appears as a seven floored pagoda that looks forged from bronze, with a quiet fire burning on top. An old Gu Immortal in Tie Yi’s build group calls Beacon Tower Tie clan’s signature Immortal Gu House and says a house formed from mortal Gu can still transport Gu Immortals. Tie Yi, a rank six Tie clan Gu Immortal, replies that overall power rises with tower count: at least one hundred towers are needed to reach Immortal Gu House power, more than one thousand already stand in Southern Border and can transport rank seven Gu Immortals, and transporting rank eights would need at least ten thousand. When one tower is destroyed, others tremble in linked feedback; Fang Yuan then destroys many in succession by combining wisdom path deduction with Fixed Immortal Travel. Shang clan’s first supreme elder treats the mortal Gu cost as low enough to rebuild after losses.

Clear Jade Dripping Wind Tiny Bamboo Building later reaches Fang Yuan’s tribulation site so fast that a watching Heavenly Court immortal credits the Beacon Towers and plans to destroy them first in any future Southern Border invasion. Fang Yuan finds the towers troublesome because they are easy to rebuild, and he notes that large scale construction came earlier in this life because of him.
